messages.author: 5f39963f076a3c4a
messages.subject: maturity of Renjin Project
parts:
Hi ,

First of , a java interpretor for R is one cool thing to think about.
Thanks for building such a innovative tool.


My company is working on providing analytic financial solution and we
were thinking of exposing a R interface for the end users to run
calculation over the time series data we store.
We would like to know how mature Renjin project is for a commercial
usage. We would like to know if the speed achieved by Java Renjin
interpretor is as good as R interpretor or better.
Also it would help to know if some company have adopted Renjin in
their system.

Thanks
Vineeth ,
Architect,
Algotree.

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: maturity of Renjin Project
parts:
Hi Vineeth,

Thanks for your interest in Renjin! At this point, renjin is not a
stage where you will be able to use seamlessly in production-- We're a
ways off from even a beta release.

That having been said, we use renjin to call a few key R packages from
java in production systems, so I'd say it is potentially suitable for
narrow, well-defined cases, but you'll need to be prepared to dive
into the code and implement/fix things necessary for your particular
use case.

Renjin's performance is creeping up towards that of C-R, particularly
if use native blas libraries, see my slides from a recent talk (http://
www.slideshare.net/AlexBertram/renjin) for a few benchmark
comparisons.

Best,
Alex

messages.author: 780c00049ff90c5e
messages.subject: Re: maturity of Renjin Project
parts:
Vineeth,

One other thing you should think about is that, when we're done with
all R primitives, our implementation will be able to do things like
open socket connections, read files on the disk, and things like that.
Giving clients the ability to have full access to the R language could
be a security vulnerability.

That being said, if this is a common use case, maybe we can separate
the primitives to two groups and have the interpreter run in safe mode
or full mode. Thoughts?

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: maturity of Renjin Project
parts:
No guarantees!   ;-) 

I would just spend some time testing it :-)

And also, Jamie is right, you may want to be careful running untrusted R code on your server. Fortunately, the ability to safely run untrusted code was a major motivation for Renjin, so there are some things in place to support this:

1) All file operations go through the Apache Commons VFS, and you can provide Renjin with your own FileSystemManager that would, for example, give only read-only access to the library files and a small read/write sandbox elsewhere. See the appengine-repl sample for how to configure this.

2) The r.lang.SecurityManager interface is also intended to give you more control over what R code can to do. At this point, there is only one permission -- allowNewInstance(class), which gives you control over which java objects can be created by R code. 

Also, I'd encourage you to use the javax.scripting interfaces as much as possible because the rest of the API *is* subject to change. 

All the best,

Alex

have in mind and identify where it currently falls short. We can then
evaluate together the level of effort it will take to close the gap,
and that will give you an approximate indication of how risky a choice
renjin is.

Best,

Alex
